newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FORECAST-San Miguel 6-mth net seen flat.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-San Miguel 6-mth net seen flat.

text.p: The good times are slowly returning for brewer San Miguel Corp but, thanks to miserable first-quarter earnings, growth for the first half of 1997 will be flat, analysts said on Friday.

A poll of five Manila stock brokers completed on Friday showed San Miguel was expected to post an average profit of 2.40 billion pesos, barely changed from 2.41 billion in the first six months of 1996.
"Their first quarter was horrible and that will cut into the six months even though things are improving," said Fred Devera, analyst at ING Barings.
The company, started more than a century ago in the district of San Miguel in the old walled city of Manila, has such a stronghold that Filipinos never order a beer. Rather, they ask for San Miguel.
But despite a name synonymous with beer, the company reported a disappointing profit of 904 million pesos in the first quarter (Jan-March) of 1997.
However, analysts said the second quarter and the rest of the year would restore some of the fizz to the beer business.
The poll predicted an average full-year net of six billion pesos, up 14 percent from last year's 5.26 billion pesos.
Figures in the poll exclude extraordinary gains.
Sales growth has fallen because of high taxation and younger people shifting to other drinks.
The company managed to pass on to customers tax-induced price increases in beer and spirits in March and its La Tondena Distillers unit is doing well.
San Miguel's soft drinks unit, Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc, has also benefited from consumers shifting away from beer.
"This unit contributes about 25 percent of San Miguel's revenue," said Spencer Yap of BPI Capital Corp.
San Miguel's first quarter net was partly blighted by a price war with rival Pepsi. To fight back, San Miguel cut the price of Coke, but the expected rise in volumes did not happen.
"But they have now reported that the rise in volumes did happen and this will show in the second quarter," Yap said.
Earlier this year, San Miguel agreed to sell Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines to Australia's Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd in exchange for a 25 percent stake in Amatil.
Of those polled, Anscor Hagedorn Securities was most optimistic on San Miguel's full-year prospects.
"We are basically counting on national elections to boost beer consumption," said Tricia Hocson of Anscor.
Campaigning for next year's presidential elections would gather momentum by Christmas and experience shows that
politicians would ply voters with beer, she added.
Analysts said San Miguel's heavy interest burden from its overseas expansion programme would continue to weigh on profits. The firm has set up breweries in China and Indonesia.
But its property unit is seen as a bulwark against the vagaries of its other businesses, including food.
One analyst, who asked not to be named, said San Miguel's first quarter net was boosted by a share placement.

San Miguel valued its office building in Manila at 1.2 billion pesos and issued what it called "HOC shares". These are exchangeable preferred shares entitling holders to shares of San Miguel Properties Philippines when it is listed.
The money from the placement saved San Miguel's first quarter, the analyst said.
